Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

tess: the pickup area is clear as of tuesday afternoon. i checked the shelf and the labeled cabinet with Omar, and neither had anything marked for Ren or Patrick. there's still one unclaimed microphone stand, but the tag says “loaner from room B,” not either former member. i don't know who owns it, so i left it where it was and messaged the equipment channel instead of adding a name to the access list.

eli: i'd leave the tape note in place until the caretaker sees it. it's attached to the desk with masking tape, not on the access clipboard, and it has the alarm company's old number plus two bin labels. i don't know if she uses those labels during the monthly inventory. if she says it's no longer useful, she can take it down; i haven't asked her yet, so please don't treat it as confirmed waste.

noor: makes sense. i'll message her about the note separately, and i'll keep that out of the access-sheet edit. one thing for the edit: the sheet has a notes column and an updated-on column, but the printed copy only has names and keyholder status. i'll add the change date and pickup details to the sheet, then print a fresh copy for the front desk after the edits are saved.

maya: small timing detail: if the north door reader is still offline by friday, leave Lena's brass-key entry active and don't switch the list to the side entrance roster. the reader was tested this morning but still flashed red twice, so facilities is coming back tomorrow. if it works before then, that doesn't change who holds the key; it only means people can use the north door again. i don't have a confirmed repair time.

tess: i can put a temporary note beside the front desk copy that says the north door reader is being checked, but i won't write a code or share one in the thread. facilities told me the side entrance is open during staffed hours, and the caretaker can let people in for scheduled deliveries. outside those hours, the current keyholder procedure still applies, so a reader issue shouldn't turn into permission for everyone to use the brass key.
